title: Policy intake sanitizer and schema fuzz harness for region/tier routing
text:
Policy intake sanitizer and schema fuzz harness for region/tier routing

description:
Refactor the initial policy intake path so incoming routing rules (region selection, tier routing, and fallback model variants) are sanitized, canonicalized, and validated before they enter the policy engine. The goal is to reduce runtime errors, improve actionable error messages for users, and make staged schema migrations safe. This includes: (1) an input sanitizer that normalizes semantically-equivalent constructs (region aliases, tier synonyms, legacy model-tag shims); (2) a canonical form emitter that feeds downstream components a single, well-typed IR; and (3) a schema fuzz harness to exercise edge-case configs against the validator and runtime mapping logic.

background:
We regularly encounter customer configs that are functionally correct but trigger runtime mismatches (e.g., region aliases like "eu-west-1" vs "ew1", tier names with minor typos, or fallback chains referencing deprecated model variants). Current validator is too permissive in some cases and too strict in others, and error messages are opaque. Previous attempted fixes patched specific failures (see ENG-4927, ENG-27134), but lack a unified intake pipeline and automated test coverage. This ticket consolidates those learnings into a single, testable intake stage and a fuzzing harness that will prevent regressions during future schema migrations.

tradeoffs_and_decisions:
1) Strict vs permissive validation: we adopt a two-stage approach — sanitizer + best-effort autofix suggestions (non-destructive) and strict canonical validation that can be enabled per-organization via a safety toggle. 2) Auto-correct behavior: sanitizer will only auto-correct low-risk cases (region aliases, harmless capitalization) and will surface suggested fixes for higher-risk changes (tier remapping, model aliasing). 3) Location of canonicalizer: implement in the intake service (pre-policy-engine) to keep runtime stateless and reduce downstream forks. 4) Performance tradeoff: canonicalization runs on write (config apply) rather than at read path to avoid token-latency impact on inference requests.

acceptance_criteria:
Intake sanitizer normalizes known region aliases and emits canonical region ids for 100% of test cases from the canonicalization spec
Validator rejects configs with ambiguous or conflicting tier rules and returns user-facing, actionable error codes with suggested fixes
Fuzz harness finds and reproduces at least five real-world config failure patterns we observed in production logs
Unit and integration tests covering sanitizer, canonical emitter, and validator are included and run in CI with >90% coverage for the new intake codepaths
Migration plan documented and a feature-flagged rollout that can be toggled per org; no user-facing failures during a canary with 5 internal teams

tasks:
Draft canonicalization spec (region aliases, tier synonyms, model alias map)
Implement input sanitizer service and API contract for downstream components
Build canonical-form emitter and type definitions (protobuf/JSON schema)
Extend validator with clear error codes and suggestion payloads
Implement schema fuzz harness and seed corpus from production config leaks and support tickets
Add CI jobs: fuzz runs nightly, unit/integration on PRs
Create migration and rollback playbook; coordinate with SRE for canary rollout
Write console UX hooks so console shows suggested autofixes and non-destructive warnings

risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: Over-eager autofix could change customer intent. Mitigation: autofix only applied in a dry-run mode and requires explicit accept before persisting; produce suggested-fix diff in audit log.
Risk: Fuzz harness produces noisy failures. Mitigation: seed harness with curated corpus and add heuristics to triage by likelihood and customer impact.
Risk: Validator changes break downstream consumers. Mitigation: maintain stable backward-compatible canonical IR; release toggles and compatibility shims for 2 release cycles.
Risk: Performance regression on config apply path. Mitigation: benchmark sanitizer end-to-end and optimize hot paths; run load test on the staging fleet before rollout.
